content.text: Truc is a 15th-century bluffing trick-taking game from France and Spain. Players get 3 cards and try to win 2 of 3 tricks. NO TRUMP and NO suit obligation â€” highest card wins regardless of suit (7 is highest in French version). Equal cards spoil the trick. Major bluffing component: players can propose to raise stakes at any point.

Truc probably originates from the end of the Middle Ages in Spain; the word means "trick" or to trick into false announcements in Valencian. It later migrated to France and is closely related to the old English game Put, first described by Cotton in The Compleat Gamester (1674). Truc is the basis of Truco, popular in Argentina, Uruguay, Venezuela, Paraguay and Brazil.
